requirements.title: The build tool shall report its name and semantic version to standard output when invoked with --version, exiting with code 0

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Version exposure
vision.paraphrase: This is a baseline tool-hygiene requirement, not derived from the vision doc — CLAUDE.md declares --version as the CLI's mechanism for exposing its version to an end user.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit a log line at startup containing its name and semantic version at INFO level

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Version stamped at log startup
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the first log line at process startup must name the tool and its version.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit log records at the levels DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR in human-readable prefixed plain-text format written to standard error

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Logging convention
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the four-level, human-readable, stderr-only logging convention for the build tool.

requirements.title: The build tool shall exit with code 0 on success, code 1 on operational failure, and code 2 on invalid invocation

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Exit code convention
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the 0/1/2 exit-code convention so calling scripts and CI can distinguish success, operational failure, and invocation errors.

requirements.title: The build tool shall reject invocation without a --vault argument with exit code 2 and a usage hint

conops.paraphrase: Every operational scenario begins by the author pointing the tool at a specific vault path — the tool has no meaningful behavior without one, so an invocation lacking --vault is an invalid-invocation case the PM persona surfaced as an implicit negative-path requirement.

requirements.title: The build tool shall write primary build output confirmation to standard output and shall write diagnostics, progress, and log output to standard error

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: stdout / stderr discipline
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares stdout carries primary/parseable output while stderr carries diagnostics, progress, and logs.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit user-facing error messages to standard error that name the problem and name the next user action

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Error message standard
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares that user-facing errors must name both the problem and the next user action.

requirements.title: The build tool shall walk every Markdown file under the vault path and parse its YAML frontmatter (title, tags, status, Related, Referenced By) into a node record

vision.paraphrase: The tool must process Markdown wiki content with structured metadata to transform raw vault files into queryable node records, supporting the graph data structure.
Vault content uses git-committed Markdown with frontmatter-driven metadata; the build tool must parse this frontmatter to extract page attributes for the graph.

conops.paraphrase: When the author points the CLI at a local vault path, the tool walks the vault to discover and parse all Markdown files, extracting their frontmatter into node records.

requirements.title: The build tool shall collapse directional Related and Referenced By frontmatter links between two pages into a single undirected edge in graph-data.json

vision.paraphrase: The graph representation collapses directional backlink relationships into undirected edges to simplify the force-directed visualization.

conops.paraphrase: During parsing, the tool synthesizes undirected graph edges from the frontmatter's directional Related and Referenced By relationships.

requirements.title: The build tool shall assign each node a folder/taxonomy value derived from the page's directory path within the vault

vision.paraphrase: Nodes must be grouped and colored by folder taxonomy to visually cluster related content in the graph.
Node color-coding by folder/taxonomy cluster organizes the graph visually to mirror content structure.

conops.paraphrase: The graph renders nodes colored by their folder/taxonomy cluster, which the tool derives from each page's directory path during the build.

requirements.title: The build tool shall skip a Markdown file with missing or malformed frontmatter, emit a WARN log identifying the file, and continue processing the remaining vault

conops.paraphrase: The tool must handle real-world messiness by gracefully skipping malformed files while continuing to process the rest of the vault.

requirements.title: The build tool shall produce zero nodes and zero edges in graph-data.json, without error, when run against a vault directory containing no Markdown files

vision.paraphrase: The 'generic point-at-a-repo tool' goal implies the tool must behave predictably across arbitrary vault states, including the degenerate case of an empty or not-yet-populated vault, without crashing.

requirements.title: The build tool shall write graph-data.json as a single valid JSON document containing top-level nodes and edges arrays

vision.paraphrase: The tool must emit a valid graph-data.json artifact containing nodes and edges that the Next.js page will fetch client-side.
Static graph-data.json is fetched client-side by the Next.js page; it must be valid JSON with nodes and edges arrays.

conops.paraphrase: The tool builds a valid graph-data.json file containing the parsed nodes and synthesized edges.
The build regenerates graph-data.json to include new pages added to the public vault.

requirements.title: The build tool shall compute a precomputed embedding for each vault page's title, body, and tags and write it to vector-index.json alongside the page id

vision.paraphrase: Build-time precomputed embeddings over page content enable real semantic search at query time without dynamic backend calls.
The tool computes build-time embeddings per page and writes a static vector-index.json asset for client-side cosine-similarity ranking.

conops.paraphrase: The tool computes embeddings per page and writes a vector-index.json file alongside graph-data.json.
The rebuild regenerates vector-index.json with embeddings for new pages.

requirements.title: The build tool shall regenerate graph-data.json and vector-index.json fully on every run, with no incremental/partial update

vision.paraphrase: Static derived artifacts (graph-data.json and vector-index.json) are regenerated fully on each build with no incremental updates.

requirements.title: The build tool shall write its output assets only to the local path specified by the user and shall never transmit vault content to any network destination

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary ensures private vault content never leaves the local machine during build.
Content isolation guarantees the tool only outputs to local paths and makes no network calls that could leak private content.

conops.paraphrase: Local iteration against the private second-brain produces output JSON assets only to the local build directory, never published.

requirements.title: The build tool shall require an explicit --vault path argument for every invocation and shall never fall back to a default or previously used vault path

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary requires explicit vault path on every invocation to prevent accidental use of wrong vault.
Input supports local filesystem path only, requiring an explicit --vault argument.

requirements.title: The deployed production build configuration shall reference a single hardcoded --vault path pointing at the dedicated public vault, with no build-time flag or environment variable able to override it

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary requires the production build configuration to hardcode the public vault path with no override capability.

requirements.title: The repository shall never contain a committed file referencing the second-brain private vault's filesystem path

vision.paraphrase: Safe-by-construction boundary prevents accidental exposure by ensuring no committed code references the private vault's path.

requirements.title: The build tool shall include newly added vault pages in graph-data.json and vector-index.json on the next run without any tool-code changes

vision.paraphrase: The tool must be generic, supporting point-at-a-repo operation without code changes as vault content evolves.
Rebuild-on-publish workflow allows new vault pages to appear in the live graph on rebuild without tool modifications.

conops.paraphrase: When new pages are added to the public vault, rebuilding the tool generates updated graph-data.json and vector-index.json automatically.

requirements.title: The build pipeline shall support producing a full Next.js static export that embeds the current graph-data.json and vector-index.json, deployable with no server runtime

vision.paraphrase: Live-feeling static graph requires a Next.js page that fetches graph-data.json client-side and renders via react-force-graph.
Build pipeline produces static assets (graph-data.json and vector-index.json) fetched client-side by the Next.js /graph page.

conops.paraphrase: The Next.js static export build packages the current graph and vector assets for static hosting.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit a description field on each node in graph-data.json sourced from that page's frontmatter description field when present

vision.paraphrase: The build tool emits a per-page description field in graph-data.json, sourced from frontmatter or falling back to the first body paragraph, enabling rich detail display in the side panel.
The rich detail panel relies on per-page description content to provide users with a 1–3 sentence summary without clicking through to the source.

conops.paraphrase: During demo-vault ingestion, authored wiki pages include description frontmatter; the build tool captures and emits these as node descriptions in the deployed graph-data.json.
When a visitor clicks a node, the side panel displays the node's description, enabling quick understanding of the page's focus without visiting the source.

requirements.title: The build tool shall fall back to a page's first body paragraph as the node description when the page's frontmatter declares no description field

vision.paraphrase: Description field fallback to the first body paragraph ensures every page carries a summary even without explicit frontmatter, providing a graceful default behavior.

conops.paraphrase: When a page lacks a frontmatter description, the build tool synthesizes one from the page's first body paragraph, ensuring the side panel always displays a description.
During ingestion, pages without explicit description fields automatically derive one from their first paragraph, reducing manual data entry.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit an empty description for a page that has neither a frontmatter description nor any body paragraph, without error and without omitting the node

conops.paraphrase: The tool gracefully handles edge cases like front-matter-only pages, emitting an empty description field rather than crashing or silently omitting the node.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit a top-level meta.sourceCount field in graph-data.json reporting the number of raw source entries ingested into the vault

vision.paraphrase: The meta.sourceCount field bridges the ingestion workflow (raw entries per source) to the deployed footer, enabling visitors to spot-check the 'built from K sources' claim.
The stats footer's 'built from K sources' figure directly powers an end-to-end transparency claim; meta.sourceCount supplies the denominator for this claim.

conops.paraphrase: After ingestion produces raw/ entries, the build tool counts them and emits meta.sourceCount in graph-data.json, surfacing the ingestion scale in the deployed footer.
The stats footer displays the sourceCount from graph-data.json's meta field, showing visitors the scale of research that seeds the graph.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit meta.sourceCount as null and continue the build when no sibling raw directory exists for the given vault path

vision.paraphrase: The tool's headline claim is that any Karpathy-pattern vault renders with no per-vault code changes. A 'raw/' sibling is this project's own convention, so its absence must be an ordinary case rather than an error, and null records that provenance is simply unknown for that vault.

conops.paraphrase: The footer's provenance clause can only be drawn when the vault declares sources. Emitting null rather than 0 lets the page distinguish 'this vault claims no provenance' from 'this vault ingested nothing', so it never renders a claim it cannot support.

amended.reason: Originally emitted 0 when no raw/ sibling existed. Reworked to emit null: 0 asserts 'ingested zero sources', a fact the tool cannot know when the directory is simply absent. The null/0 split is consumed by TOR-08-dkecfj5, which omits the footer's provenance clause in both cases. Not a change-control event — the TOR was authored this cycle and is unmerged.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit meta.sourceCount as 0 when a sibling raw directory exists for the given vault path but contains no Markdown files

vision.paraphrase: Pins the honest reading of an empty but present raw/ directory: the vault does declare a provenance location, and what it holds is genuinely zero, which is a different fact from declaring none at all.

conops.paraphrase: Separates the two no-provenance cases feeding the footer so the data layer stays truthful, even though both render identically to the visitor.

requirements.title: The build tool shall extract standard inline Markdown links from a page's body into a sourceLinks field on that page's node entry in graph-data.json

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Body Source Links, Cycle 4)
vision.paraphrase: The build tool scans each page's Markdown body for standard inline links in `[text](url)` form and captures up to 5 found, in document order, storing them as sourceLinks in graph-data.json.

The graph-data.json field sourceLinks stores an array of up to 5 `{ text, url }` pairs extracted from standard `[text](url)` Markdown links found in the page body, in document order, independent of wikilinks and the GitHub self-link.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a node whose page body contains standard `[text](url)` links, those links appear in the side panel as a distinct cited-sources list.
Body source-link discovery occurs when a visitor clicks a node whose page cites external material inline, surfacing up to 5 of those citations extracted from the page body.

requirements.title: The build tool shall cap the sourceLinks field at the first 5 inline Markdown links found in a page's body, in document order

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Body Source Links, Cycle 4)
vision.paraphrase: The build tool captures up to the first 5 inline `[text](url)` links found in document order, enforcing a hard cap to keep the cited-sources list concise.
The sourceLinks array is capped at 5 entries per page, preserving document order from the body scan.

conops.paraphrase: The cited-sources list shown in the side panel displays up to 5 links from the page body, in the order they appear, never exceeding this cap.

requirements.title: The build tool shall not extract wikilinks as sourceLinks entries, keeping body source-link extraction distinct from Related/Referenced By edge parsing

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Body Source Links, Cycle 4)
vision.paraphrase: Wikilinks (`[[slug|title]]`, used for Related/Referenced By edges) are a different syntax from inline Markdown links (`[text](url)`) and are never picked up by sourceLinks extraction.
SourceLinks extraction is parsed independently of the existing Related/Referenced By wikilink parsing, preserving the distinct purposes of each syntax.

conops.paraphrase: During the build, two separate parsing passes occur: one synthesizes undirected edges from wikilinks, and the other extracts external citations from body-link syntax; these do not interfere with each other.

requirements.title: The build tool shall not deduplicate repeated URLs when extracting sourceLinks, counting each occurrence toward the 5-link cap

vision.paraphrase: When a link is cited multiple times in a page's body, each occurrence is recorded separately in the sourceLinks array; no deduplication occurs, and each instance counts toward the 5-link cap.

conops.paraphrase: The cited-sources list faithfully represents what the author wrote: if a link appears twice, it appears twice in the list (within the 5-link cap), preserving the page's original emphasis.

requirements.title: The build tool shall emit an empty sourceLinks array, without error, for a page whose body contains no inline Markdown links

vision.paraphrase: Pages with no inline body links get an empty sourceLinks array in graph-data.json, allowing the side panel to cleanly omit the cited-sources section without error.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a node whose page has no inline Markdown links, the cited-sources section is not rendered, and the build tool exits cleanly.

requirements.title: The build tool shall extract [[Page Name]] wikilinks found anywhere in a page's Markdown body as graph edges, not only within '## Related' or '## Referenced By' sections

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Generic wikilink extraction
vision.paraphrase: The tool generalizes edge discovery beyond this project's own bespoke heading-gated convention so it works against real-world Obsidian/PKM vaults that scatter wikilinks freely through ordinary prose without such structure.

conops.paraphrase: When a third-party vault owner points the tool at their Obsidian vault, the build tool scans each page's full body for wikilinks anywhere in prose and resolves them to graph edges.

requirements.title: The build tool shall produce at least the same edge set for a vault using the '## Related'/'## Referenced By' body-section convention as the previous heading-gated extractor produced

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Backward-compatible with existing vaults
vision.paraphrase: The generic full-body wikilink scan is a strict superset of the old heading-gated scan, ensuring no vault migration is required for existing second-brain or ai-adoption-wiki content.

conops.paraphrase: The generalized parser maintains backward compatibility: when applied to this project's own vaults with their bespoke Related/Referenced By sections, it produces the same edges as before.

requirements.title: The build tool shall resolve a [[Page Name]] wikilink against any note in the vault whose filename or frontmatter title matches, case-insensitively, regardless of folder

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Title/filename link resolution
vision.paraphrase: Wikilinks resolve by filename or title match rather than exact slug path, enabling the tool to work with real-world Obsidian vaults where note organization doesn't follow a rigid path convention.

conops.paraphrase: When processing a third-party vault, wikilinks are resolved against any note whose filename or frontmatter title matches, case-insensitively, reflecting Obsidian's own resolution behavior.

requirements.title: The build tool shall resolve an ambiguous wikilink — one matching more than one note's filename or title — to the first such note encountered during the vault walk, deterministically

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Backward-compatible with existing vaults
vision.paraphrase: Deterministic resolution of ambiguous wikilinks ensures consistent results across runs, a prerequisite for backward compatibility and reproducible graph generation.

conops.paraphrase: When multiple notes match a wikilink target, the tool deterministically selects the first one encountered in the vault walk, ensuring consistent results across multiple builds.

requirements.title: The build tool shall recognize '![[Page Name]]' embed syntax and exclude it from graph edges

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Embeds excluded from edges
vision.paraphrase: Embed syntax represents inline content transclusion, not a relational reference, so it must be explicitly excluded to distinguish embeds from actual wikilinks in edge extraction.

conops.paraphrase: When scanning a third-party vault's body content, embed syntax is recognized and correctly excluded from the graph's edge set.

requirements.title: The build tool shall silently drop a wikilink whose target note does not exist in the vault, logging the skip at DEBUG level only

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Unresolved links handled gracefully
vision.paraphrase: Unresolved wikilinks are treated as ordinary data-quality variations, not errors—they are dropped silently and logged only at DEBUG level to keep the build reliable across real-world messy vaults.

conops.paraphrase: When a third-party vault contains wikilinks pointing to nonexistent notes, the tool silently drops them with DEBUG-level logging, allowing the build to complete successfully without false errors.

requirements.title: The build tool shall assign a neutral 'unknown' status to a node whose page frontmatter declares no status field, without error

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Optional status field
vision.paraphrase: The status field becomes optional so third-party vaults without it still build successfully, with nodes rendering a neutral/unknown status dot instead of causing a build error.

conops.paraphrase: When a third-party vault contains no status frontmatter on any page, the build tool assigns a neutral/unknown status to each node and completes successfully.

requirements.title: The build tool shall normalize a page's tags frontmatter written as a comma-separated or space-separated string into the same tags array shape used for YAML list tags

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Normalized tag shapes
vision.paraphrase: Tags are accepted in multiple formats (YAML array, comma/space-separated string) and normalized to a uniform array shape, allowing the tool to accept vaults with varied frontmatter conventions.

conops.paraphrase: When scanning a third-party vault's frontmatter, the tool normalizes tags written as comma or space-separated strings into the same array shape used internally.

requirements.title: The build tool shall extract inline '#hashtag' tags from a page's Markdown body and merge them into that page's tags array

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (Vault-parsing Generalization, Cycle 5): Normalized tag shapes
vision.paraphrase: Tags found as inline hashtags in page bodies are extracted and merged into the normalized tags array, accommodating vaults where tags are authored as free-form body hashtags.

conops.paraphrase: The tool scans each page's body for inline hashtags and merges them into the frontmatter tags, accepting tags in multiple authorship styles.
